items.title: Stock Radar: Divi’s Laboratories stock hits fresh record high in July 2026; time to book profits or buy the dip?
items.description: Divi's Laboratories stock reached a new record high in July 2026. Chart patterns indicate continued upward momentum for the pharma stock. Short-term traders can consider buying the stock for a target of 8,000 levels. The stock has shown significant gains over recent weeks and months. Experts recommend buying with a stop loss below 6950 levels.

items.title: India's private banks draw thinner margins on tepid credit growth
items.description: Top private sector banks reported weaker net interest margins (NIMs) in the June quarter as sluggish retail loan demand pushed them towards lower-yielding corporate loans. HDFC Bank's NIM fell to 3.26%, Kotak Mahindra Bank's dropped to a 19-quarter low of 4.53%, while Axis Bank's stood at 3.46%.

items.title: Indian banks mobilise $20.7 billion under RBI's special incentive window
items.description: In a remarkable financial boost, India's central bank recorded significant foreign exchange inflows of $20.72 billion, primarily through a swap facility provided by the Reserve Bank of India. Out of this amount, Foreign Currency Non-Resident Deposits accounted for $17.41 billion. Meanwhile, External Commercial Borrowings contributed $1.34 billion, and Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings brought in an additional $1.97 billion, enhancing the country’s economic standing.

items.title: Alpine Texworld shares to debut today; GMP signals muted listing
items.description: Alpine Texworld shares:  The stock is expected to debut with only a marginal gain, as the grey market premium stands at about 1%, implying a listing price of around Rs 106 against the upper issue price of Rs 105. The IPO, which was open from July 14 to July 16, was subscribed 1.40 times overall, reflecting moderate investor demand.

items.title: Premier Energies among 5 stocks closed above VWAP, signalling bullish shift
items.description: On July 20, the closing prices of five stocks in the Nifty500 pack rallied more than 1.5% above their Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP), according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A move above the VWAP suggests a potential bullish trend, as it indicates that the stock is trading above its average price for the session after accounting for trading volumes.When the closing price rises above the VWAP, it means the closing price is higher than the average price at which the stock traded throughout the day, with the average weighted by trading volume. Traders and investors often interpret this as a bullish signal, reflecting positive market sentiment and the possibility of continued upward momentum.

items.title: Union Bank of India among 7 stocks flashing bullish signals, hinting at a possible uptrend
items.description: On July 20, seven stocks in the Nifty500 appeared on the 'White Marubozu' bullish scanner, according to StockEdge's technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period and the closing price is the highest.Represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and a small or nonexistent lower shadow, it indicates strong buying pressure throughout the session. Traders interpret it as a signal that buyers were in control from the opening to the closing, often using such patterns to assess the potential continuation of upward momentum.

items.title: PNB among 4 stocks showing bullish RSI upswing
items.description: On July 20, four stocks from the Nifty500 segment that gained over 3.5% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.com. An uptrend signal is generated when the RSI value crosses above 50 from lower levels.“RSI trending up” indicates that Relative Strength Index (RSI) values are rising, suggesting strengthening momentum in the stock’s price action. This can indicate potential upward movement and is often used by traders to identify buying opportunities in momentum-driven markets.

items.title: SBI Funds Management gets 2 buy calls before listing. Why Equirus, Emkay see up to  31% upside
items.description: The firms have set target prices of Rs 675 and Rs 750 for March and June 2027, implying an upside of up to 31% from the IPO issue price of Rs 574.

items.title: SBI Funds Management IPO to list today; GMP signals 17% premium debut
items.description: Ahead of the listing, SBI Funds Management shares are commanding a Grey Market Premium (GMP) of around Rs 97. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band at Rs 574, the GMP points to an estimated listing price of nearly Rs 671, implying a potential 17% listing gain for investors.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 13 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs
items.description: In the Nifty500 pack, 13 stocks' closing prices crossed above their 200 DMA (Daily Moving Averages) on July 20, 2026, according to stockedge.com's technical scan data. The 200-day daily moving average (DMA) is a key indicator traders use to determine the overall trend in a particular stock. As long as the stock is priced above the 200-day SMA on the daily timeframe, it is generally considered to be in an overall uptrend. Take a look:

items.title: Triveni Engineering demerger: Last day to buy stock to get Triveni Power Transmission shares. Check details
items.description: The company, which is associated with the production of sugar and ethanol along with engineering works, announced earlier this year that as part of its demerger of its power transmission business, every eligible shareholder get one share of Triveni Power Transmission for every three shares held in Triveni Engineering as on the record date.

items.title: Sebi imposes Rs 1 crore fine on CDSL
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India fined CDSL one crore rupees. This penalty addresses cybersecurity and operational lapses following a malware attack. The depository failed to adequately secure critical systems, which disrupted operations. CDSL's systems were isolated from the market after the incident. No monetary penalty was imposed on former top officials.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Equity markets faced pressure as Nifty declined, while broader markets showed gains. Analysts expect sideways to mixed trading due to geopolitical tensions and oil prices. The Indian rupee weakened to its lowest level in two months on Monday. India VIX, a fear index, saw a slight decrease settling at 12.98. Stock-specific action is anticipated as the Q1 earnings season progresses.

items.title: Stocks in news: CDSL, Adani Energy, L&T, Adani Total Gas, Emcure Pharma
items.description: Markets declined on Monday due to disappointing earnings and geopolitical worries.  CDSL faced a Rs 1 crore penalty from Sebi for cybersecurity lapses.  Several companies will announce their first quarter financial results today.  Grasim Industries invested Rs 74,000 crore in capital expenditure over five years.  Larsen & Toubro secured multiple mega orders for its metals business.

items.title: Strong Q1 sets stage for FY27 growth as UltraTech bets on cables business
items.description: UltraTech Cement reported its strongest first quarter volume and profit ever.  Near-term performance faces monsoon seasonality and higher input costs.  The company anticipates double-digit volume growth in the next fiscal year.  Its new cables and wires business will launch in the third quarter.  Lower stock valuation offers a cushion against potential downside risks.

items.title: Private banks go for a tumble on D-St after Q1 stumble
items.description: Most private lender stocks declined Monday after first-quarter earnings showed profitability pressures. Axis Bank and HDFC Bank saw significant drops, while ICICI Bank gained. Analysts noted margin compression as a key factor affecting banking stocks. Foreign investors returned to financials after substantial withdrawals earlier in the year. ICICI Bank remains a top pick among leading private sector lenders.

items.title: First Bell: SBI Funds' investors in line for 10-15% listing pop
items.description: SBI Funds Management's stock is anticipated to debut at a premium of ten to fifteen percent.  The company's initial public offering was subscribed over forty-one times on its final day.  Analysts suggest investors can book profits or hold shares for long-term gains.  The IPO price valued SBI Funds Management at over one lakh crore rupees.  This listing is expected to narrow the valuation gap with its listed peers.

items.title: Coal India subsidiary CMPDI shares climb 7% after Q1FY27 profit surges 54% YoY
items.description: CMPDI shares jumped nearly 7% after the Coal India subsidiary reported strong Q1FY27 results, with revenue rising 18% and net profit surging 54% year-on-year. Robust operational growth and the announcement of a Rs 1.05-per-share interim dividend further lifted investor sentiment.

items.title: HDFC Bank shares fall for 2nd day but Jefferies, others brokerages remain bullish. Should you buy the dip?
items.description: HDFC Bank shares extended losses for a second straight session after its Q1 FY27 earnings, but brokerages remain optimistic on the stock. Jefferies, Motilal Oswal, Nomura and JM Financial have retained their bullish ratings, with target prices implying upside of up to 35% from current levels.

items.title: ​Axis Bank among 5 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of July 20, there was a notable surge in futures open interest for five stocks in the NSE F&O pack, contributing to a total increase in open interest of over 6% as compared to the previous trade. A significant uptick in futures open interest signifies a substantial growth in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a specific security. This uptrend reflects an increasing number of participants either initiating new positions or expanding the size of their existing positions within the futures market.

items.title: PNB shares jump 7% in 2 days after Q1 earnings. Should you buy, sell or hold?
items.description: Punjab National Bank shares have surged in the last two sessions after the PSU lender reported a 214% year-on-year jump in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 5,253 crore, prompting bullish brokerage calls. Net interest income rose 2% to Rs 10,798 crore.

items.title: Mrs Bectors Food shares surge 30% in 4 days after Sunil Singhania's Abakkus acquires 1% stake. Do you own?
items.description: Mrs Bectors Food shares extended their four-day rally to nearly 30% after Abakkus Investment Managers acquired a 0.96% stake through a bulk deal. The stock hit a five-month high of Rs 219.61, supported by investor interest and steady March-quarter growth in revenue and profit.

items.title: MTAR Technologies falls 5%, extends 4-day slide to 20%
items.description: MTAR Technologies shares hit the 5% lower circuit for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, taking their four-day decline to nearly 20% and one-month loss to 31%. The sell-off came as promoter and mutual fund holdings declined in the June quarter. However, foreign institutional investors raised their stake to 24.80% from 17.31%, signalling stronger overseas participation.

items.title: Karur Vysya Bank shares soar 11% after stellar Q1 results. What investors should know
items.description: Karur Vysya Bank shares rose sharply after the private lender posted a 45% year-on-year jump in Q1 net profit to Rs 756 crore. Strong growth in net interest income, an improved net interest margin, healthy loan and deposit growth, and stable asset quality lifted investor sentiment.

items.title: SBI Funds Management shares list at 7% premium, but target prices go up to Rs 750. Time to buy?
items.description: SBI Funds Management Share Price: SBI Funds Management debuted with a nearly 7% premium over its IPO price, falling short of grey market expectations. Despite this, brokerages remain bullish, with Emkay assigning a Rs 750 target price and Equirus Rs 675, while analysts advise long-term investors to hold the stock on strong fundamentals.

items.title: Jaiprakash Power shares surge 8% after Q1 profit jumps 69%, revenue rises 12% YoY
items.description: Jaiprakash Power shares rallied 8.4% after strong Q1FY27 results, with revenue rising 12.2% and profit surging 68.6% year-on-year. The company returned to sequential profitability, while increased institutional holdings and positive technical momentum further supported investor sentiment.

items.title: ICICI Bank wins analysts’ vote after Q1 show; HDFC Bank, Axis, Kotak & Yes Bank face scrutiny
items.description: ICICI Bank shares rose after reporting strong June quarter earnings and improved financial metrics. Other major private lenders like HDFC Bank and Axis Bank saw their stock prices decline. Analysts favored ICICI Bank for its consistent performance and clean results this quarter. Kotak Mahindra Bank also received a buy recommendation with a watchful eye on leadership. Investors are advised to consider their risk appetite when choosing among these banking stocks.

items.title: Dixon Tech shares down 30% from 52-week high. Can these 3 triggers reignite the rally for 79 lakh shareholder
items.description: Dixon Technologies shares may see a rally after recent declines from their peak. Government approval for the Vivo joint venture is a significant development for smartphone manufacturing. New policy support for electronics manufacturing aims to boost domestic production and global competitiveness. Expanded customs duty exemptions are expected to lower input costs for the company. These combined factors strengthen Dixon's growth outlook and shareholder value.

items.title: Cause for concern? HDFC Bank is lagging ICICI Bank where it matters as investors count Rs 5 lakh crore loss
items.description: HDFC Bank's stock has declined significantly this year, losing considerable investor value. Analysts note a widening operating gap between HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. Margins are under pressure for HDFC Bank, while loan growth lags peers. ICICI Bank shows stronger earnings, better margins, and faster credit growth. Investors await margin recovery and management stability for HDFC Bank.

items.title: UltraTech Cement shares gain 2% after Q1 results. Why Nuvama, other brokerages raised target?
items.description: UltraTech Cement shares rose after the company posted a 17% year-on-year rise in Q1 FY27 consolidated net profit to Rs 2,599 crore and a 16% increase in revenue to Rs 24,648 crore. The stock also gained after multiple brokerages raised their target prices, encouraged by strong earnings and management guidance

items.title: Paytm shares gain 3% after Q1 results. What are Goldman Sachs, Citi and CLSA saying?
items.description: Paytm shares rose 2.7% after the fintech firm reported a 79% year-on-year jump in Q1 consolidated net profit to Rs 220 crore. Revenue from operations increased 28% to Rs 2,448 crore, while total income rose 22% to Rs 2,630 crore. Profit before tax climbed to Rs 247 crore, reflecting stronger operating performance both year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter.

items.title: South Korea’s Kospi jumps 4% after 31% crash from June peak. What’s ahead?
items.description: South Korea's Kospi index saw a significant jump, recovering some losses after a sharp decline. Shares of chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix drove this recent market recovery. However, the index remains in a bear market, reflecting investor caution and wild swings. Authorities have intervened to cool speculative fever and curb leveraged trading. Analysts suggest foreign investor selloffs are moderating, with a neutral stance on the market.

items.title: Sensex falls over 50 points, Nifty below 24,250 despite Iran-US mediation efforts
items.description: Indian stock markets saw marginal losses on Tuesday as Sensex and Nifty traded flat. Broader markets, however, opened with modest gains, bucking the overall trend. Mediation efforts between Iran and the US led to a dip in oil prices below $90 per barrel. Analysts suggest crude oil prices and banking sector earnings will guide market direction. Geopolitical developments and regional tensions remain key factors influencing market sentiment.

items.title: Which listed companies contributed to Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 success?
items.description: Skyroot Aerospace's successful Vikram-1 orbital mission has spotlighted the listed companies supporting India's private space ecosystem. From early investor Solar Industries to technology partners Inox India, TechEra Engineering and Diffusion Engineers, these firms have played key roles in Skyroot's journey toward becoming a global private launch player.

items.title: MFs kept buying these 14 stocks for 3 quarters; shares surged up to 101%
items.description: Over the past three quarters, mutual funds (MFs) have steadily increased their holdings in around 156 companies from the BSE 500 universe, using September 2025 as the base period. Retail investors often track the moves of large institutional investors like MFs, whose investment decisions are backed by extensive research. Among these companies, around 26 stocks in which MFs consistently raised their stakes delivered gains of more than 25% over the past year. Notably, 11 of these stocks surged between 50% and 101%, including one multibagger that more than doubled investors’ wealth within 12 months. (Data Source: ACE Equity).

items.title: Alpha Wealth 2.0: Why some investors keep finding the next opportunity before everyone else
items.description: The best advantage is not information, but perspective. With wealth creation going beyond traditional investing. Discover why investors are reconsidering capital allocation, portfolio strategy and long-term wealth creation and how the Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0 is facilitating these conversations.

items.title: MSCI India rejig: Eternal likely to see highest inflows at $648 mn; Lenskart, Groww among Nuvama’s expected inclusions
items.description: MSCI’s August India Standard Index review could trigger major passive inflows, with Eternal expected to attract the highest at $648 million, according to Nuvama. The brokerage sees Laurus Labs, Adani Energy Solutions, Lenskart and Groww among likely inclusions, while Balkrishna Industries, SBI Cards and Astral face potential exclusions.

items.title: Risk is integral to the market; but there are different kinds of risk: 6 mid-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 21%
items.description: We are in uncertain and volatile times. Does that mean investors should just sit out the downturn? While that is an option, the better option is to use the current drawdown as an opportunity to pick up stocks of good businesses. And how do we define a good business? It is one with three clear attributes.

items.title: TVS Motor shares jump 6% after Q1 net profit soars 67% YoY to Rs 1,019 crore, revenue up 33%
items.description: TVS Motor Company's net profit surged sixty-seven percent year-on-year to one thousand nineteen crore rupees. Revenue from operations also increased thirty-three point five percent to sixteen thousand two hundred ninety-five crore rupees. The company's board approved raising up to one thousand crore rupees through debt instruments. Highest quarterly EBITDA of one thousand seven hundred seventy-nine crore rupees was reported. Overall two and three-wheeler sales grew twenty-eight percent during the quarter.
